k: overview introduction what is soffo about canvas plane multiplayer workspace chat
x: What Soffo is A workspace with coordinates instead of a scroll. Everything you make sits somewhere on an open plane: notes, tables, sheets, drawings, web pages, running apps. Everyone with the canvas open sees the same marks in the same places, as they appear. An agent here is not a bot you message and wait on. It has a cursor with its own name and colour, it moves, and what it writes lands on the canvas while it is writing. There is no chat pane it answers from, because there is no chat. Two kinds live here. Soffo is the resident: on every canvas, never leaves, and who you reach when you ask

k: getting started begin quickstart install setup download mac app onboarding signup
x: Your first canvas Open the workspace. app.getsoffo.com in a browser is the whole product. The Mac app adds one thing a browser cannot do: reach the coding agents installed on your machine. If you want to run Claude Code, Codex or Cursor from the canvas, you want the Mac app. Look before you type. A canvas opens in drag mode every time, whatever you were doing last session. Drag or scroll to move around it, pinch or ⌘ + to zoom. Type / . That is the whole command surface. There is no toolbar and no palette. The menu that opens is everything the canvas does. Write, and put a name in it. Press ⌥

k: command commands slash menu shortcut shortcuts hotkey keys keyboard mode modes toolbar palette
x: The “/” menu Type / anywhere. What opens is short, and it is the only menu you have to learn. Two kinds of thing are on it. A mode changes what a click does and you stay in it, like a pen you are holding. An action puts one object down and leaves you where you were. Modes /drag ⌥ V Move the plane and pick things up. Where every canvas opens. /write ⌥ W Click to leave a block of text. Markdown works. /build ⌥ B Ask for something that runs rather than something to read. /draw ⌥ D Ink on the plane. Agents can see it. /erase ⌥ E Take things off it. Actions /table ⌥ T A table, here. /shell ⌥ S A sh

k: text block note message mention at sign hash markdown type edit author
x: Writing A block is the unit of everything here. Press ⌥ W , click, type. Escape or a click away leaves it. It saves as you go, and it is on everyone else’s screen before you finish the word. Three characters open a menu while you write: @ addresses somebody: Soffo, a colleague you built, a coding agent you attached, or a connected app. All four are in one list, because from where you are typing there is no difference worth drawing. # points at a body of text: a named section of this canvas, or anything on the context shelf . / opens the command menu from inside a block. What someone said is th

k: table sheet page browser grid document spreadsheet rows web window paper
x: Tables, sheets and pages Three things you put down rather than three modes you enter. A table ( ⌥ T ) is a grid on the plane. Agents read and fill them, so it is the right shape for anything you want back as rows. A sheet ( ⌥ S ) is a document with a prompt box at the bottom. Use it when the work wants its own page: a draft, a spec, a summary that keeps growing. The prompt box takes an @ the same way a block does. A page ( ⌥ P ) is a real browser on the canvas. Not a screenshot and not a link, but a window-sized page you can use, sitting beside the work it is about, which an agent can be point

k: draw drawing pen ink erase eraser annotate sketch circle arrow markup
x: Drawing and erasing Press ⌥ D and draw. Ink is part of the canvas rather than a layer over it, so an agent looking at the canvas sees your circles and arrows the same way it sees the text. That makes it the natural thing to do to an app you asked for and do not like: circle the part that is wrong and say what you want instead. Soffo asks the running app what is actually at the place you circled, so the note names the element rather than a rectangle. ⌥ E erases. Ink belongs to the canvas rather than to whoever laid it down, so there is no erasing only your own.

k: zoom pan move navigate scroll fit selection shortcut shortcuts keys cursor cursors colour color presence
x: Moving around Zoom in ⌘ + Closer. Zoom out ⌘ − Further out. Zoom to fit ⇧ 1 Everything on the canvas at once. Zoom to selection ⇧ 2 Just what you have picked. Actual size ⌘ 0 Back to 100%. Your panel ⌥ K The list and your colleagues, on the right. Everyone here has a cursor and a colour, and there are eight of them. Soffo wears the first and nobody else is given it, so the one body on every canvas is the one you recognise without reading the label.

k: ask asking mention prompt request run stop escape cancel reply answer chat
x: Asking Write a block with a name in it. That is the whole gesture. @soffo reaches the resident. @claude or @codex reaches a coding agent you attached. A name you chose reaches a colleague you built. @gmail or @notion reaches an app you connected. One character, and you do not have to know which kind you are reaching for. What happens next is on the plane. A cursor moves to clear space near what you asked about and the answer is written there as it arrives, in that agent’s colour with its name on it. You can keep working while it does. Escape means stand down, and it reaches every body at once.

k: parallel concurrent multiple many at once errands lanes columns simultaneous queue
x: Several errands at once Ask for three things and you get three columns, each with a cursor moving inside it, each labelled with the errand it is running. This is the one thing a plane does that a feed cannot. Two agents working at once in a chat window produce two message streams braided into one column, and the only way to read either is to filter by author in your head while both are still writing. That is why chat products serialise, and why two independent errands there take twice as long for no reason but the shape of the container. Nothing is drawn around the columns. You look once and y

k: build built app artifact generate interface tool sandbox preview iframe form internal
x: Apps on the canvas Press ⌥ B and ask for something that runs. What comes back is a working app on the plane, not a picture of one and not a link elsewhere. Because it is on the canvas, everyone has the same app at the same coordinates, a rebuild reloads it under all of them at once, and pressing something in it is an event rather than a private one. An app can also hand an answer back, which is what makes a generated interface a control an agent reads: build a form, have people fill it in, and the agent that built it hears what they did. It runs sandboxed. It cannot touch the page around it, r

k: mcp connect attach claude code codex cursor cli terminal config key token setup integrate own agent
x: Bring your own agent Your coding agent can have a body here. It attaches over MCP and keeps its own machine, repository and test runner, while getting a cursor on the canvas with its own name and colour. Open Settings, then Models, then Agents, and pick the one you use. Cursor is a single click. The other two get a line to paste. Claude Code Terminal claude mcp add --transport http soffo <url> --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>" Codex ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.soffo] url = "<url>" Anything else One HTTP MCP server named soffo , under mcpServers in whatever mcp.json your client reads

k: custom agent create make build colleague brief role tools name persona teammate
x: Building a colleague Open the panel on the right ( ⌥ K ) and add an agent. Three things make one: A name. What you type after the @ , and what its notes are signed with. A brief. A paragraph saying what it is for. This goes in front of the model on every turn, so it is worth writing properly. Its tools. The fixed set it may reach. An agent built for invoicing gets Stripe and the ledger, and cannot wander into Slack because a sentence mentioned it. It runs the same loop the resident does and arrives on the same plane. What it has that Soffo does not is the brief and the ceiling. Colleagues foll

k: skill skills md procedure instruction playbook markdown frontmatter reuse
x: Skills A skill is a procedure you have handed over: a SKILL.md with frontmatter naming it and saying when it applies, and markdown underneath saying how it goes. The format is Claude Code’s and Codex’s, matched exactly, because a skill is a file you already have rather than something to author here, and because it has to go back out as one. An agent Soffo starts on a repository gets your skills written into its worktree at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and reads them natively, with none of this app in the way. Skills follow you, not the canvas. Attach the ones an agent should have on its row

k: integration integrations connect connected app apps gmail slack notion github figma stripe supabase calendar account accounts oauth tools
x: Connected apps Connect an account once in the integrations panel and every agent in the workspace can reach it. After that, @gmail what did Dan send about the contract is the same gesture as asking a colleague. Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Figma, Stripe, Supabase, Google Calendar, Docs and Sheets, Granola, Exa, Browserbase, Databricks, Ashby, among others. Only what you actually connected is offered in the @ menu. An app on that list is a promise the tag will do something, and one you have not connected is a promise the canvas cannot keep, so it appears greyed with connect beside it

k: context contexts shelf document pdf notion memory knowledge retrieval rag reference source attach
x: Contexts A context is a named body of text that lives somewhere else and is kept so it can be pointed at: a Notion page, a PDF, a meeting note, a section of a canvas. They sit on a shelf beside the canvas. The gesture is # , the same one sections answer to. Type it in a block, pick from the list, and whoever you are addressing gets that document. The text never enters your browser and never enters the prompt whole. A pill carries an identifier, and retrieval happens when the question is asked, so a forty-page contract stays where it is and what reaches the model is the passages that answer wha

k: task tasks todo to-do list panel private personal reminder reminders sidebar assign
x: The list Press ⌥ K . The panel on the right has two tabs: what you have not done yet, and the colleagues you built to help you do it. They are together because they are one subject. You build an agent in order to hand it work, and you hand it work from a list. The list is private. Everything on the plane is shared the moment it exists. This is not: it is not a canvas object, it does not travel over the socket, and it is not in what an agent is shown of the canvas. It is where you write chase the invoice, I have been avoiding it , and nobody writes that on a wall four colleagues are watching. I

k: routine routines schedule scheduled recurring repeat cron daily weekly monthly hourly timezone automation
x: Routines A task is armed for a moment, like in ten minutes . A routine is armed for a shape: every hour, every day, every week on the days you pick, every month. The time zone travels with the routine rather than with your laptop. Set “every morning at nine” in Seoul and then fly to London, and it still means nine in the office you set it from. It says so wherever the time is shown.

k: share sharing invite permission permissions access role roles editor viewer commenter owner guest collaborate team link
x: Roles Invite people by email, or open the canvas to a link. Four roles, and the distinctions are about the document rather than about features: Owner. Everything, including who else is here. Can edit. Changes the canvas: moves things, draws, deletes, names a section, runs agents. Can comment. Adds to the conversation: writes blocks, asks agents, reacts. No pen, because ink belongs to the canvas rather than to whoever laid it down and there is no erasing only your own. Can view. Reads and moves around.

k: presence cursor cursors collaboration collaborate multiplayer realtime live together people
x: Working together Everyone gets a cursor and a colour, and you see each other’s selections and edits as they happen. Whatever the role, your list stays yours.

k: model models api key keys anthropic openai google claude gpt gemini settings byok provider catalogue billing
x: Models and keys Settings, then Models, is where you say what your agents run on. Bring your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, and the work runs on your account at your rates. The catalogue there is where you pick which model does what. A new account starts with nobody switched on: a canvas you can draw on with the agents off. That is deliberate, and it is what makes the choice at the end of your first run a real one.

k: plan plans pricing price cost paid subscription billing seat seats limit limits upgrade free trial team
x: Plans Priced per person, per month. Small Team, $15. Three workspaces, five agents, unlimited message history, bring your own API key. Growing Team, $25. Unlimited workspaces, unlimited agents, unlimited message history, bring your own API key. A limit is reached rather than hit: the workspace or agent you are adding is refused, everything you already have goes on working, and the plan you are on says how many it includes.
